stem: What distinguishes public cloud from private cloud?

choices.A: Provider services available to multiple customers
choices.B: No networks are permitted
choices.D: All data is anonymous

explanations.A: Public cloud serves logically separated customers.
explanations.B: Public cloud provides networking.
explanations.C: Public providers operate infrastructure.

stem: A cloud environment is dedicated to one organization. Which model is this?

choices.B: Private cloud
choices.D: SaaS

explanations.B: Dedicated use characterizes private cloud.
explanations.C: Serverless describes an operating abstraction.

stem: What defines hybrid cloud?

choices.B: Two services in Azure
choices.C: A public service with a private IP but no private environment
choices.D: Integration of public and private cloud environments

explanations.B: Multiple services alone are not hybrid.
explanations.C: Private addressing alone does not make a deployment hybrid.

stem: An Azure database uses a private endpoint. What deployment model does it retain?

choices.B: SaaS solely due to the endpoint
choices.D: On-premises server

explanations.A: Private connectivity does not change Azure's provider model.
explanations.B: Networking does not select service model.
explanations.C: Addressing does not transfer ownership.

stem: Can a third party operate a private cloud for one organization?

choices.B: Yes, dedicated use is the key property
choices.C: Only if all data is public
choices.D: No, an employee must operate it

explanations.A: That is unrelated to private-cloud operation.
explanations.B: Private operation can be outsourced.
explanations.C: Public data is not required.
explanations.D: Private clouds can use external operators.

stem: A company uses Azure and another public provider. Which term directly fits?

choices.A: Hybrid cloud solely because there are two providers
choices.B: Private cloud
choices.D: Single public cloud

explanations.A: Two public providers indicate multicloud, not necessarily public-private integration.
explanations.B: Two public providers do not imply private cloud.
explanations.C: The organization uses multiple providers.

stem: Which conclusion does not follow from public-cloud hosting?

choices.A: Multiple customers may use the provider
choices.B: Customers can consume capacity
choices.D: Everyone can read customer data

explanations.B: Capacity consumption is part of the offering.
explanations.C: That fits public-cloud delivery.
explanations.D: Public tenancy does not remove authorization.

stem: Why is a privately owned ordinary server not automatically private cloud?

choices.B: Only storage can be private cloud
choices.D: Cloud capabilities such as on-demand provisioning still matter

explanations.B: Compute can also be offered.
explanations.C: Internet exposure is not required.
explanations.D: Ownership alone does not supply a cloud operating model.

stem: A private environment and Azure support one integrated workload. What model fits?

choices.B: Multicloud solely because two environments exist
choices.D: Public cloud only

explanations.A: The scenario defines deployment, not a finished app.
explanations.B: The decisive fact is integrated private/public environments, not multiple providers.
explanations.C: The combined solution spans private and public environments.
explanations.D: That omits the retained private component.

stem: Which categories describe deployment environments?

choices.B: Hot, cool, and archive
choices.D: Reader and Contributor

explanations.B: These classify blob access tiers.
explanations.C: These classify service responsibility.

stem: What is needed for confidential information in public cloud?

choices.A: Moving provider servers into the office
choices.B: Appropriate authorization and governance
choices.D: Removing identity checks

explanations.A: Azure use does not require this.
explanations.B: Customer data still needs access controls.
explanations.C: Public offerings do not require public information.

stem: Which fact best supports describing a workload as hybrid?

choices.A: Both environments use identical VM sizes
choices.B: Components integrate across private and public environments
choices.C: The public side has an invoice
choices.D: Both environments have separate applications with no connection

explanations.A: Matching sizes do not establish integration.
explanations.B: Hybrid concerns a combined solution.
explanations.C: Billing does not prove integration.
explanations.D: Separate usage alone does not demonstrate an integrated hybrid workload.

stem: Which property is compatible with private cloud?

choices.B: Prohibition on automation
choices.D: Organization-dedicated capacity and access

explanations.B: Cloud operations can be automated.
explanations.C: Data ownership is not defined this way.

stem: Which statement separates deployment model from exposure?

choices.A: Internet exposure turns private cloud into SaaS
choices.B: An Azure app can have restricted access in public cloud
choices.C: A public IP proves public-cloud ownership
choices.D: A private IP proves private cloud

explanations.A: Exposure does not define a service model.
explanations.B: Provider deployment and network access are separate.
explanations.C: Private environments can also expose public services.
explanations.D: Azure VNets also use private IPs.

stem: A startup wants launch speed without datacenter maintenance. Which model is a suitable starting point?

choices.B: Offline-only local server
choices.D: Public cloud

explanations.B: That does not meet the cloud launch requirement.
explanations.C: The scenario gives no need for a private component.

stem: A factory retains a private system and integrates an Azure portal. Which model matches?

choices.B: SaaS as a deployment model
choices.D: Public cloud only

explanations.A: The solution combines retained private and public components.
explanations.B: SaaS classifies the service boundary.
explanations.C: That fails the integration requirement.

stem: What should guide cloud-model selection for regulated data?

choices.A: An assumption that public cloud forbids sensitive data
choices.B: Only the lowest advertised compute rate
choices.C: Verified residency, access, and compliance constraints
choices.D: A blanket belief that dedicated hosting is always mandatory

explanations.A: That is an unsupported blanket claim.
explanations.B: Cost alone does not establish compliance.
explanations.C: Actual requirements should drive placement.
explanations.D: Mandatory placement must follow actual requirements.

stem: Which requirement supports considering private cloud?

choices.A: A short test needing provider capacity today
choices.B: Avoiding all infrastructure operation
choices.D: Verified need for organization-dedicated infrastructure control

explanations.B: Private environments retain more operating work.
explanations.C: Exposure does not require private cloud.
explanations.D: Dedicated control matches the private model.

stem: What needs consideration in a hybrid design?

choices.A: A belief that private hardware has no cost
choices.B: Integration, security, staffing, and costs across both sides
choices.C: Only the public component's VM price
choices.D: An assumption that connection is automatic

explanations.B: Coordinated operation covers both environments.
explanations.C: Hybrid operation includes private-side and integration costs too.

stem: The only private dependency is retired. What should happen to the hybrid recommendation?

choices.A: Reassess whether a private component remains necessary
choices.B: Keep it because architecture cannot change
choices.D: Declare all Azure resources private cloud

explanations.A: Changed requirements can change the model.
explanations.B: Decisions should follow current requirements.
explanations.C: Retiring a dependency does not remove security needs.

stem: A manager chooses public cloud to publish confidential records. What needs clarification?

choices.A: Private cloud makes every user trustworthy
choices.B: Hosting model and data-access policy are separate
choices.D: Only hybrid can authenticate

explanations.A: Private hosting does not guarantee user behavior.
explanations.B: Public-cloud use does not authorize publication.
explanations.C: That misunderstands tenancy.
explanations.D: All deployment models can support authentication.

stem: Which question matters for a local latency-sensitive dependency?

choices.A: Can the app tolerate measured cloud-network delay?
choices.B: Are all regions physically identical?
choices.C: Does a private endpoint automatically place the app next to the factory?
choices.D: Can a discount commitment eliminate network latency?

explanations.B: Regions occupy different locations.
explanations.C: Private addressing does not relocate the application.
explanations.D: Pricing discounts do not remove physical/network delay.

stem: Why consider public cloud for seasonal demand?

choices.B: Obtain capacity without owning all peak hardware
choices.D: Remove all code maintenance

explanations.B: Provider delivery can support variable needs.
explanations.C: Capacity use does not change provider ownership.

stem: Which choice preserves required local investments while adding Azure capability?

choices.A: Move everything immediately regardless of dependencies
choices.B: Assume local apps are already SaaS
choices.D: Integrate retained private components with suitable Azure services

explanations.B: Local placement does not define finished software.
explanations.C: Automation can help either environment.

stem: What tradeoff should accompany organization-dedicated private-cloud control?

choices.B: No future cost
choices.D: Automatic access to every Azure region

explanations.A: Users and permissions still require management.
explanations.B: Dedicated capacity still costs money.
explanations.C: Control comes with infrastructure and staffing needs.
explanations.D: Private scope depends on actual implementation.

stem: What evidence should precede moving a private app to Azure?

choices.B: A promise that no changes are ever needed
choices.C: An assumption that all licensing transfers
choices.D: Only proof that both environments can store files

explanations.B: Apps may require changes.
explanations.C: License terms must be checked.
explanations.D: Basic storage capability does not prove application compatibility.

stem: What should override an otherwise convenient cloud choice?

choices.B: The region with the lowest rate despite failing residency rules
choices.C: The deployment model already used by an unrelated workload
choices.D: The provider with the most product categories regardless of fit

explanations.B: A mandatory residency requirement outweighs a cheaper incompatible choice.
explanations.C: Another workload's choice does not override this workload's constraints.
explanations.D: Product count does not satisfy mandatory workload requirements.

stem: A small team evaluates private cloud. What cost assumption should it avoid?

choices.B: Workload constraints matter
choices.C: Private cloud is necessarily cheaper overall
choices.D: Public providers supply services

explanations.B: Constraints should drive the decision.
explanations.C: Dedicated infrastructure and operation need costing.

stem: Which choice makes a deployment decision reviewable?

choices.A: Choose one model for every workload blindly
choices.B: Choose solely by private IP usage
choices.C: Document the decisive constraint and tradeoff
choices.D: Treat deployment models as access roles

explanations.B: Addressing does not define cloud model.
explanations.C: The rationale can be checked against requirements.

stem: An organization considers hybrid only because two teams use Azure. What is missing?

choices.B: A public resource with restricted internet access only
choices.C: A private component integrated with the public environment
choices.D: A second subscription in the same public cloud alone

explanations.A: Hybrid does not require public data.
explanations.B: Restricted public-cloud access does not supply an integrated private component.
explanations.C: Two Azure teams alone do not establish hybrid.
explanations.D: Multiple subscriptions do not establish public-private integration.
